name: quality-audit
description: Quality / test-coverage audit: per-area analysis of bugs, UX issues, security gaps, incomplete features and untested code, anchored to the coverage reports left by tests/coverage.sh; screened, then written to docs/audit/<date>.md.

phases.task:
Quality audit of area **{item.area}** in this repo (read CLAUDE.md first for the architecture).

Code: {item.code}
Existing tests: {item.tests}
Focus: {item.focus}

Coverage summary:
{steps.coverage.output}

Line-level coverage is in target/cov/lcov.info (Rust; `SF:` file, `DA:<line>,<hits>`) and web/coverage/lcov.info (PWA). Grep them for this area's files to find uncovered functions/branches — do not read the whole file.

Read the area's code and its tests. Report findings in these categories:
- bug: wrong/unexpected behaviour (state the input and the wrong result)
- ux: confusing, inconsistent or missing feedback (CLI/TUI/PWA), silent failures, data-loss-prone interactions
- security: trust-boundary problems (auth, tokens, input from network/files, path handling, secrets on disk)
- incomplete: features that are stubbed, half-wired (e.g. API exists but no UI, TODOs, dead config keys) 
- untested: user-visible behaviour with zero or trivial coverage (cite uncovered lines/functions)

Rules: every finding needs concrete evidence `file:line` you actually read; no speculation about code you did not open; prefer fewer, verified findings over a long list. Max 12 findings.

Output ONLY a JSON array (no prose, no code fence):
[{"area":"{item.area}","severity":"high|med|low","category":"bug|ux|security|incomplete|untested","title":"...","evidence":"path:line[, path:line]","detail":"what/why, 1-3 sentences","repro":"steps or command, or empty","suggested_test":"which suite (unit/blackbox/playwright) + what it asserts"}]

Security review of the network-facing surface of this repo (read CLAUDE.md first): crates/mgmt-web (all of it), crates/mgmt-sync/src (HttpRemote, ics.rs subscription fetch, pairing), crates/mgmt-cli/src/web.rs, web/src/api.ts, web/src/lib/notify.ts.

Coverage summary (what the e2e suites exercise):
{steps.coverage.output}

Static pass: auth guard ordering and public-route list, session cookie attributes, bearer token scoping between users, feed-token comparison, rate limiter keying (X-Forwarded-For), TOTP replay, invite/pairing URL secrets, ICS/subscription SSRF + size/timeout, path traversal in asset serving and ICS import, admin-only routes, SSE resource exhaustion, secrets written to disk with wrong modes, CSRF on cookie-authenticated mutating routes.

Live pass (do it): start `target/cov/debug/mgmt --data-dir $(mktemp -d) web serve --bind 127.0.0.1:0` (no --no-auth; it prints the URL) in the background, and with curl probe: unauthenticated access to every /api route, admin routes as a non-admin bearer, cross-user access via /api/sync tokens, malformed JSON/oversized bodies, path traversal on static assets, feed token guessing (404 vs 401), login brute-force behaviour. Kill the server when done. Note in each finding whether it was confirmed live.

Output ONLY a JSON array (no prose, no code fence) of findings:
[{"area":"security","severity":"high|med|low","category":"security","title":"...","evidence":"path:line","detail":"...","repro":"curl ... (or empty)","suggested_test":"suite + assertion"}]
An empty array is a valid answer if nothing is found.

Write the audit report to `docs/audit/{args.date}.md` (create the directory; if the file exists, overwrite it). Structure:

# Quality audit {args.date}

## Coverage
The summary below, as a compact table (Rust per-crate line % + total; PWA total). Note how to regenerate (`just cov`).

{steps.coverage.output}

## Findings
One `###` per finding, ordered high→med→low, each with: severity + category badge, evidence (`file:line`), detail, repro (if any), suggested test. Group nothing by area — severity order only, but keep the `area` in the heading, e.g. `### [high][security][web-auth] ...`.

## Test gaps (untested category) — a table: area | what | suggested suite.

## Dropped during screening — a short table title | why.

Findings JSON:
{steps.screen.output}

Do not invent findings, do not soften severities, keep prose terse. After writing, reply with only: the file path, the count of findings per severity, and the three highest-priority items as one line each.
